flags: Wise Group plc completed its dual listing and transferred its primary listing to Nasdaq. It became the ultimate parent of Wise Limited through a Scheme of Arrangement.

The company announced a share buyback program of up to £405 million (approximately $540 million) of Class A ordinary shares. Weekly 6-K notices show repurchases still under way in November 2026, with the shares held in treasury.
Wise Europe, the Belgian subsidiary, reached an agreement to fully resolve and settle the Brussels prosecutor's inquiry, with no admission of wrongdoing.

business_model.claim: Wise sells cross-border money movement and multi-currency account services to three customer groups: individuals (Wise Account), small and medium-sized businesses (Wise Business), and banks, financial institutions and enterprises (Wise Platform).
quotes: We market our services through three product offerings: Wise Account for personal customers, Wise Business for small and medium-sized businesses, and Wise Platform for banks, financial institutions and enterprises.

business_model.basis: stated in P3; absence of segment tables is inferred from the excerpts provided
business_model.claim: Wise manages and reports its revenue by revenue stream, not by product offering. The filing excerpts name no separate reporting segments.
quotes: We evaluate and manage our revenue principally based on these net revenue streams rather than by individual product offerings.

business_model.basis: stated in F2 income statement and the P3 results table
business_model.claim: Net revenue is transaction revenue plus interest income on customer balances, less interest expense on customer liabilities. In the year to March 31, 2026, transaction revenue was 1,893.6 (table in millions), up from 1,546.3. Interest income on customer balances was 806.1 and net revenue was 2,502.8, up from 2,098.9.

Cross-border revenue is a percentage fee on volume, so growth depends on volume, active customers and the take rate. In the year to March 31, 2026, cross-border volume rose to $243.5 billion from $185.2 billion, and active customers rose to 18.9 million from 15.6 million. The average take rate fell to 0.52% from 0.58%.
quotes: Cross-border take rate is calculated as cross-border revenue divided by cross-border volume.

business_model.basis: stated in P3; H1 figures stated in the P8 results table
business_model.claim: Management deliberately passes efficiency gains to customers as lower prices, which pushes the take rate down. In H1 FY27 the take rate was 0.50% against 0.52% a year earlier, while net revenue rose to 1,453.1 (table in $ million) from 1,183.8.
quotes: Our commitment to a return-led approach means we continue to pass on efficiency gains and sustainable reductions in our costs to our customers as price reductions, driving our long-term growth and reducing our take rate.

business_model.claim: Interest income on customer balances depends on the size of customer deposits and market interest rates. Wise returns only part of this income to customers: it returned 45% of its target share in the year to March 31, 2026, partly because of regulatory restrictions such as those in the United Kingdom.
quotes: Interest income on customer balances is affected by the amount of customer deposits we hold and market interest rates.

business_model.claim: Customer money is a very large part of the balance sheet. At March 31, 2026, funds payable and amounts due to customers were 30,254.2 (table in millions) of total liabilities of 31,334.6, against cash and cash equivalents of 27,802.2.
Card revenue, mainly interchange and card usage fees, is a smaller revenue stream, at 16% of net revenue in the year to March 31, 2026.
quotes: which was 16% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026

business_model.claim: Wise Business represented about one quarter of transaction activity and Wise Account the rest. Wise Platform was less than 10% of overall transaction activity and is counted inside those two. Management's long-term aim is for Platform to exceed 50% of cross-border volume.
quotes: Wise Platform does not yet generate a material percentage (i.e., it currently generates less than 10%) of the Group’s overall transaction activity
Our long-term aim is for Wise Platform to account for more than 50% of Wise’s cross-border volume.

growth_thesis.claim: Cross-border volume growth is the main driver. Volume rose to $243.5 billion from $185.2 billion in the year, and the latest half-year volume was 141.0 against 113.9 (table in $ billion), up 24%. For this to continue, customers must keep choosing Wise for cross-border transfers and volume must keep growing faster than the price cuts take away.

growth_thesis.claim: Growth in active customers underpins the volume growth. Active customers rose from 15.6 million to 18.9 million. For this to continue, Wise must keep and add licenses and keep capacity to onboard new customers.

Our customer growth is dependent on our ability to maintain existing and obtain new licenses, as well as maintaining capacity to onboard new customers.

growth_thesis.claim: Price reductions are used to win volume. The average cross-border take rate fell from 0.58% to 0.52%. For this to continue, efficiency gains must keep funding lower prices without making unit economics worse.
quotes: Our commitment to a return-led approach means we continue to pass on efficiency gains and sustainable reductions in our costs to our customers as price reductions, driving our long-term growth and reducing our take rate.
